extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions applying for IES (Institute of Education Sciences) education research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used to evaluate IES education research grant applications, including the four major review criteria (Significance, Research Plan, Personnel, Resources), SEER principles, and WWC evidence standards. Targets applicants preparing proposals and reviewers assessing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the applicant make a compelling case for the potential contribution of the project to the solution of an education problem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For development projects: Present a strong rationale — including a theoretical foundation and prior empirical evidence — justifying the development of the selected intervention or assessment. Emphasize the potential contribution to solving an educational problem and the importance of the outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the research design and appropriateness of methods to address the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider: quality of the research design; appropriate methods to address the research questions; sample size and analysis plan; plan for data analysis and interpretation; validity (internal and external); reliability of measures. Provide clear plans for analyses, interpretation, and threats to validity, and justify sample sizes and measurement quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications and time commitment of the principal investigator and key personnel, and the expertise relevant to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe PI and team qualifications, relevant expertise, and demonstrate adequate time commitments to deliver the proposed work. Show that the team collectively has methodological and substantive expertise necessary for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and adequacy of resources to support the project, including institutional commitment and access to data, sites, and populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional support, access to necessary data and research sites, and availability of other resources needed to complete the research. Explain how resources/sites/populations will be secured and sustained for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Excellence in Education Research (SEER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and recommended practices to encourage rigorous, transparent, and actionable education research focused on meaningful outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEER encourages research that is transparent, actionable, and focused on meaningful outcomes. Recommended practices include: pre-registering studies; making findings, methods, and data open; addressing inequities in learners' opportunities; identifying interventions' components; documenting treatment implementation and contrast; analyzing interventions' costs; using high-quality outcome measures; facilitating generalization of study findings; and supporting scaling of promising interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Process Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural aspects of how applications are reviewed and what reviewers are instructed to consider during evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Science oversees peer review. Funding opportunity announcements (RFAs) include 'Recommendations for a Strong Application' for each review criterion; peer reviewers consider these recommendations alongside their professional judgment. Reviewers apply the four major review criteria (Significance, Research Plan, Personnel, Resources) and the RFA-specific recommendations when scoring applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) Evidence Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Study-level evidence ratings used by the WWC to evaluate educational interventions, which influence what evidence IES recognizes as causal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WWC Study Review Protocols rate studies as: 'Meets WWC Standards Without Reservations' (typically randomized controlled trials with low attrition), 'Meets WWC Standards With Reservations' (quasi-experimental designs meeting WWC requirements), or 'Does Not Meet WWC Standards'. These ratings affect the degree to which a study provides causal evidence for an intervention's effects.
